STANZA I
With earnest longings of the mind
With earnest longings of the mind,
My God, to thee I look;
So pants the hunted hart to find
And taste the cooling brook.
The psalm it sets
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 42:1–5, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul longs after You, O God. 2My soul thirsts for God, the living God. When shall I come and appear in God’s presence? 3My tears have been my food both day and night, while men ask me all day long, “Where is your God?” 4These things come to mind as I pour out my soul: how I walked with the multitude, leading the procession to the house of God with shouts of joy and praise. 5Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him for the salvation of His presence. PSALM 42:1–5 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 42
